brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (0,0) and (1,0) with a 3-compartment and a 2-compartment bin that hang on the rims. Top covers are fitted over them, and the bins sit under the covers.
Notch drawer frame at (0,1) between the two bases. I did not add a separate drawer insert, and the configurator offered none.
Handle on the top cover of cell (0,0). It is off-centre on a two-cell build, so it may not balance when full.
Open faces capped and joints locked. check_build shows meshClash clear with no issues.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell organizer with two bins, a notch drawer and a top handle. It has 32 parts and is estimated at about 1.7 kg of filament. I added no props. Load capacity is not checked, and the configurator knows nothing about the print material.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
